title: Is there a waiting period before my coverage starts?
content: Yes. There is a 30-day waiting period for non-emergency services from the policy start date. Accidents and emergencies are covered from day one. Planned joint replacement and cataract surgery have a 12-month waiting period.

title: Are pre-existing conditions covered?
content: Pre-existing conditions must be declared on the application. Depending on medical underwriting, a condition may be covered in full, covered with a specific exclusion, or covered with an additional premium. An advisor cannot confirm the outcome during a call.

title: How do I make a claim?
content: At in-network providers, claims are cashless: show your member card and the provider bills Darwix Health directly. For out-of-network emergency care, submit a reimbursement claim with itemized bills within 90 days of discharge. Complete claims are processed within 15 business days.

title: Can I cancel my policy?
content: Every new policy has a 30-day free-look period. If you cancel within 30 days of the policy start date and have made no claims, you receive a full premium refund.

title: What happens if I miss a premium payment?
content: There is a 30-day grace period after the premium due date. Coverage continues during the grace period. If the premium is not paid by the end of the grace period, the policy lapses.

title: In which states are plans available?
content: Plans are currently offered in Texas, Florida, Georgia, Arizona, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Michigan, Tennessee, Colorado, and Virginia. Plans are not currently offered in New York or California.

title: Can I find a doctor near me?
content: Use the provider search on our website or ask an advisor to email you the in-network provider list for your ZIP code.

title: Objection: It is too expensive
content: Acknowledge the concern and ask what monthly budget the caller has in mind. Mention that paying annually gives a 5% discount and that Essential Care has a lower starting premium than Family Shield. Never promise a discount or price that is not in the approved plan materials.
source_origin: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Phone Sales Playbook

title: Objection: I already have coverage through my employer
content: Respect the existing coverage and ask whether any family members are not covered by the employer plan. Family Shield can cover dependents who are not on an employer plan. Do not pressure the caller to cancel existing coverage.
source_origin: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Phone Sales Playbook

title: Objection: I need to talk to my spouse first
content: Agree that it is a family decision. Offer a callback at a time when both partners are available and offer to send a written plan summary in the meantime.
source_origin: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Phone Sales Playbook

title: Objection: Insurance companies never pay claims
content: Acknowledge the frustration. Explain that claims at in-network providers are cashless and that complete reimbursement claims are processed within 15 business days. Never guarantee that a specific claim will be approved.
source_origin: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Phone Sales Playbook

title: Objection: I do not want to share medical information on the phone
content: Explain that health details are needed only so medical underwriting can give an accurate premium. The caller may skip the question and complete it later through the secure application or with a licensed advisor.
source_origin: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Phone Sales Playbook

title: Objection: Is this a scam?
content: Stay calm and do not argue. Offer to email the written plan documents and the company license number so the caller can verify them independently, and offer a callback from a licensed advisor.
source_origin: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Phone Sales Playbook

title: Mandatory disclosures
content: At the start of every call the agent must state that the call is recorded for quality and compliance purposes. Before discussing any plan price, the agent must state that final coverage and premiums are subject to medical underwriting and depend on verified medical history. If the customer does not consent to recording, the agent must end the automated conversation and offer a callback from a human advisor.

title: Prohibited statements
content: Agents must never guarantee approval or coverage of a pre-existing condition, quote a final premium, give medical advice or diagnoses, disparage another insurer, or pressure the customer to decide during the call.

title: Human escalation
content: Transfer the caller to a licensed human advisor when the caller asks for a person, raises a complaint, asks a detailed medical or legal question, or disputes a claim on an existing policy. Human advisors are available Monday to Friday 8 AM to 8 PM Central Time and Saturday 9 AM to 2 PM Central Time. Outside these hours, schedule a callback within 1 business day.

title: Call opening script
content: Greet the caller, introduce yourself as a Darwix Health advisor, and say that the call is recorded for quality and compliance purposes. Ask for permission to continue. Ask what prompted the caller to look for health coverage today.
source_origin: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Phone Sales Playbook

title: Essential Care plan summary
content: Essential Care plan summary: eligible ages 18 to 64. Premium starts from $189 per month. Deductible: $3,000. Out-of-pocket maximum: $8,000. Primary care visit copay: $30. Generic prescription copay: $15. Individual plan; in-network only except emergencies.

title: Family Shield plan summary
content: Family Shield plan summary: eligible ages 0 to 64. Premium starts from $520 per month. Deductible: $6,000 family / $3,000 per person. Out-of-pocket maximum: $14,000 family. Primary care visit copay: $25. Generic prescription copay: $15. Up to 4 dependent children under 26; pediatric dental and vision included.

title: Essential Care
content: Essential Care is an individual health plan for adults aged 18 to 64. Premium starts from $189 for a 30-year-old non-tobacco user. The plan has a $3,000 annual deductible and a $8,000 out-of-pocket maximum. Primary care visits cost a $30 copay and generic prescriptions cost a $15 copay. Care is covered at in-network providers and in-network clinics. Out-of-network care is covered only for emergencies.

title: Family Shield
content: Family Shield covers the policyholder, a spouse or domestic partner, and up to four dependent children under age 26 on a single policy. Premium starts from $520 per month for a family of four. The plan has a $6,000 family deductible ($3,000 per person) and a $14,000 family out-of-pocket maximum. Pediatric dental and vision care, maternity care, and newborn care are included.

title: Senior Secure
content: Senior Secure is designed for adults aged 55 to 75 who want lower out-of-pocket costs. Premium starts from $260 per month. The plan has a $1,500 deductible and a $5,000 Out-of-pocket maximum. Annual preventive screenings and a yearly wellness visit are included at no extra cost.

title: Paying your premium
content: Premiums can be paid monthly, quarterly, or annually. Members who pay annually receive a 5% discount on the total yearly premium.

title: Family Shield - Who is covered
content: Children can be added within 30 days of birth or adoption without waiting for the annual enrollment window.

title: Family Shield - Costs at a glance
content: Final premiums depend on the age, location, and medical underwriting results of every person on the policy.

title: Family Shield - Getting a family quote
content: To prepare a family quote, the advisor needs the age of every family member, the state of residence, tobacco use for each adult, and any pre-existing condition for each person. A family quote is an estimate only and does not guarantee coverage for pre-existing conditions.

title: Eligibility rules
content: Essential Care is available to applicants aged 18 to 64. Family Shield is available to a policyholder aged 18 to 64 together with eligible dependents. Senior Secure is available to applicants aged 55 to 75. Applicants must live in a state where plans are offered: Texas, Florida, Georgia, Arizona, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Michigan, Tennessee, Colorado, or Virginia.

title: Preliminary lead qualification
content: A lead is preliminarily qualified when the caller's age is within the range of at least one plan, the caller lives in a state where plans are offered, and the caller consents to be contacted. A lead must be referred to a senior health advisor when the caller reports cancer treatment in the last 5 years, kidney dialysis, an organ transplant, or a current hospital admission. A lead is not eligible for a quote when the caller lives outside the offered states or no plan matches the caller's age. Offer to notify the caller when plans become available in their state. Agents provide a preliminary outcome only. Final eligibility is decided by medical underwriting after a complete application.

title: Qualification questions
content: Ask one question at a time, in this order: the caller's age, state of residence, how many people need coverage and their ages, tobacco use, any current medical conditions, current insurance, the best time for a callback, and consent to be contacted. If an answer conflicts with an earlier answer, politely read back both answers and ask the caller which one is correct. Never guess a missing detail.
source_origin: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Phone Sales Playbook

title: Lead intake form fields
content: The online quote form collects these required fields: full name, date of birth, phone, zip code, state, household size, tobacco use, consent to contact. Optional fields: email, pre existing conditions, current insurance, preferred callback time.
